10.0.s.en: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

10.0.0.en: Sheba: an independent kingdom in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, which is present-day Yemen, but the Ethiopians consider that this queen was their queen and that she married Solomon and bore him a son whom she called Menelik, who was the father of the kings of Ethiopia, among them Candace, queen of Ethiopia (Acts 8:27). And Christ calls her the queen of Teman, that is, of the south (Lk 11:31), because her country lies south of the people of Israel. She is an example of the Gentiles who accepted the faith in the Old Testament (Lk 11:29, 32). Concerning the name of the LORD: that is, all of Solomon's wisdom and wealth is attributed to God.

10.0.1.en: The queen of Sheba heard much about Solomon, and about his wisdom, his knowledge and his wealth, and that he was a godly man of God, so she came herself to Jerusalem, not believing what she had heard about him, and she put questions to him to make sure of his wisdom. Perhaps they were questions in different fields, religious, administrative and scientific.

10.0.2.en: If you hold fast to God, He is glorified in you and you become a light to the world. So take care of your relationship with God, so that you may be a good image of Him and people may see God in you.

10.1.0.en: The queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem with a huge caravan of camels loaded with gifts of spices, much gold and precious stones, and she met King Solomon and laid her questions before him.

10.2.0.en: Solomon had the satisfying, convincing answer to all her inquiries, and he was not unable to answer any of the matters she put to him.

10.3.0.en: There was no more spirit in her: she was overwhelmed and greatly astonished.

10.3.1.en: When the queen of Sheba saw the greatness of Solomon's gifts and his wisdom in building the Temple and organizing the service in it, and the administrative arrangements surrounding it, from the officials of his palace and the beauty of their clothing, and his servants who were always present to serve him, and his keeping of the ordinances of his Law by offering the burnt offerings in the Temple, deep amazement and exceeding astonishment came over her.

10.3.2.en: If the queen of Sheba came to Solomon from far away to see his wisdom, are you concerned to come to the Church to see the power of Christ in His Sacraments and to lift up prayers before Him, so that you enjoy abundant blessings and are satisfied with His love?

10.4.0.en: Before what she saw with her own eyes, she could do no other than acknowledge before the king the truth of all she had heard about him and his wisdom while she was in her own country, before she came to Jerusalem.

10.5.0.en: She confessed to him that when she first heard the reports about him she doubted their truth because of their greatness, but when she came and saw and looked into matters herself, she realized that what she had heard did not amount to half of what she saw. Perhaps she also asked Solomon about the Lord when she found Solomon offering his sacrifices and his worship with great reverence, so she was moved and her heart began to accept faith in God.

10.6.0.en: The queen praised Solomon for his greatness, which his men who stand before him and his servants who serve him enjoy seeing, and she blessed the Lord his God, who loved him and set him on the throne of Israel, for it was out of the Lord's love for His people Israel that He set over them a wise king like him to lead them with wisdom and justice; and the queen of Sheba's blessing the Lord shows that she had begun to believe in Him.

10.7.0.en: The queen gave Solomon the gifts she had brought, which were 120 talents of gold, the same quantity that Hiram had given Solomon (ch. 9:14), and many spices and precious stones. The spice she brought and gave to King Solomon was very abundant, exceeding in quantity all the spice that had come to Solomon. Solomon here is a type of Christ, and the gifts of the queen of Sheba are a type of the gifts of the Magi.

10.8.0.en: Almug wood: one of the precious woods, and it has a sweet fragrance.

10.8.1.en: In addition to what the queen of Sheba presented, King Hiram's ships brought much gold from "Ophir," and also almug wood in great quantities and precious stones too. Solomon used the almug wood to make railings for the stairs of the house of the Lord and his palace, and he also made from it harps and psalteries for the singers. And there came no such almug trees, nor were seen, to the day of the writing of this book.

10.9.0.en: Solomon gave the queen of Sheba many gifts, including everything she asked of him, as a sign of friendship between their two countries, and added to it all that the generosity of kings bestows, and she turned and went back to her own country, she and her retinue.

10.9.1.en: If the queen of Sheba was greatly moved by Solomon's wisdom and arrangements and wealth, how much more are our hearts amazed when we contemplate the greatness of Christ and His wisdom and wealth and His infinite power, for He is able to give us everything and solve all our problems and protect us from every error.

10.9.2.en: The queen of Sheba came from the ends of the earth when she heard of Solomon's wisdom .. so what is our striving to know Christ and enjoy fellowship with Him? How great is the striving of our prayers and fasts and readings? What is the extent of our persistence and our seeking toward Him?

10.9.3.en: And the queen of Sheba presented many gifts to Solomon .. so what do we present to our Christ? Not material gifts only, but rather our hearts and our time.

10.9.4.en: The queen of Teman took care to ask Solomon many questions in order to benefit from his wisdom, and we who know the weakness of our understanding, do we seek Christ the Word, who is the source of wisdom for the whole world, and consult Him in all our works with many prayers?

10.10.s.en: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

10.10.0.en: A talent of gold = about 34 kilograms.

10.10.1.en: The traffic of the merchants: the merchants used to pay gold to Solomon as customs and transit fees for the trade routes that he had set up.

10.10.2.en: The kings of Arabia and the governors of the country: what is meant is the countries that Solomon subdued and that surrounded his country, and they paid him tribute. The governors of the country may also mean the leaders of the children of Israel who paid taxes to Solomon.

10.10.3.en: The weight of the gold that Solomon obtained in one year was about 23 tons. This is apart from the much gold that the merchants of the countries subject to him presented to him, and likewise the kings and rulers of those lands, which was presented to him as tribute that they were obliged to pay periodically and regularly, so his annual income from it was beyond count. In addition, the abundance of trade and the residence of merchants in the land of the children of Israel brought the country much money, in return for their residence and their business, which increased the gold and prosperity in the country. But the six hundred sixty-six talents of gold were not an annual income; rather, in one of the years Solomon obtained this quantity.

10.10.4.en: This shows Solomon's excessive concern and love for money, and all this gold was carried off by Pharaoh Shishak, king of Egypt, five years after Solomon's death (ch. 14:25, 26; 2 Chr 9, 12:2-11). For godliness with contentment is great gain. So, my brother, do not be occupied with money, for it is passing away, and if you have money, thank God for it but do not cling to it, for security and happiness are from God.

10.11.0.en: Target: a shield that the soldier carries to ward off arrows and spears from his chest.

10.11.1.en: Beaten gold: hammered gold, that is, shaped and worked by hammering.

10.11.2.en: (The shekel: 11-15 grams.) Shield: armor, a long guard that protects the soldier's body along its length.

10.11.3.en: Pounds: plural of mina, which is 100 shekels.

10.11.4.en: The target that the soldier carried to defend himself was made in that time of wood and covered with a layer of leather, but Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold, and the weight of the gold used in each target was 7 kg; he also made 300 shields of beaten gold, and the gold used in each shield was 3 kg. And he hung the targets and shields for adornment, as was the custom in ancient times, on the walls of the house of the forest of Lebanon, which he had built before.

10.11.5.en: Targets and shields are defensive means that the soldier uses, so they declare that Solomon defends the right and the oppressed, and is not like the Romans, whose procession was led by axes and rods, which represent violence and attack and the oppression of others.

10.12.1.en: Solomon made a magnificent throne, made of ivory and overlaid with pure gold, and one went up to the throne by six steps. The throne had a round top behind, and perhaps there was a canopy above the seat, with a support behind the seat in which were fixed two armrests on its sides around the place of sitting, and two lions standing beside the armrests. The two lions proclaim the power of God that was with Solomon, so that he fears no one and justice is carried out in his kingdom with all strength (see the picture of the judgment seat at the end of the book).

10.13.0.en: Solomon set twelve lions on the six steps, six on each side, so the throne was more magnificent than any throne of the kings in that age. The twelve lions proclaim to the twelve tribes that they should trust in the power of God that is with them and walk in justice and strength and fear no one.

10.14.0.en: The drinking vessels and all the other vessels that were in the king's palace and in the house of the forest of Lebanon were all made of pure gold, and none of them was made of silver, for silver had no value because of its abundance in the time in which Solomon reigned.

10.15.0.en: Tarshish: it is Tartessus, located in the south of Spain near Gibraltar, and it was a city very rich in mineral wealth.

10.15.1.en: Apes and peacocks: they were among the costly things, and importing them represented luxury in Solomon's life. Solomon had a commercial naval fleet that he built in cooperation with King Hiram, and their ships sailed the seas and went to "Tarshish" and other coastal cities, and returned once every three years to their bases on the coasts of Israel carrying gold and silver and ivory and apes and peacocks, and unloaded their cargo there. Tarshish was considered the last country of the known ancient world before the discovery of the Americas, that is, Solomon's ships passed by all the important trading countries in the world. Thus Solomon's stature grew greater than all the kings of the earth, for he surpassed them all in wealth and wisdom.

10.16.0.en: Delegations from all parts of the inhabited world used to come to the land of Israel seeking to see King Solomon and to hear his wisdom, which God had given him.

10.16.1.en: And Solomon's greatness surpassed that of the greatest countries of the world existing at that time, namely Egypt and Assyria.

10.16.2.en: Solomon used the wisdom he received in managing the affairs of government and carrying out great building works and reviving trade with all the peoples. May we too use the gifts that God has given us for the benefit of ourselves and others. Each of us God has endowed with many gifts, so let us use them in the service of our brethren and our Church, and not live for ourselves alone.

10.17.0.en: The visitors who came did not come empty-handed, but came with gifts that varied among vessels of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses and mules, and the visits were repeated from year to year, and their bringing gifts yearly implied their submission to him, for it was regarded as tribute that they had to pay.

10.18.0.en: Chariots: that is, war chariots and civil ones drawn by horses.

10.18.1.en: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, so he had 1400 chariots and 12 thousand horsemen, and Solomon distributed them among the storehouses that he had set up before in the chariot cities, and kept some of them in the capital of his kingdom, Jerusalem.

10.19.0.en: Silver in Jerusalem was regarded as stones are regarded, in terms of its abundance and its being everywhere, that is, it had no value, just as the precious cedar wood, because of its plenty, became worth no more than the very cheap sycamore wood.

10.20.0.en: Linen yarn (what was brought): that which is brought in, that is, imported, from other countries.

10.20.1.en: The Syrians: peoples living in different places, the most important of which is the region of present-day Syria.

10.20.2.en: Solomon used to import horses from Egypt, and the king's merchants obtained them at cheap prices because of Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter, so a war chariot was bought for about seven kg of silver and a horse for two kilograms of silver. The merchants used to re-export some of them to the kings of the Hittites and the Syrians, and so gained from the difference in price, and this is the meaning of his saying "they brought them out by their means."

10.20.3.en: Solomon's acquiring horses in abundance is contrary to the Law, for God commanded not to multiply them, so that man would not rely on his strength and would not be occupied with the world (Deut 16:17-20). Solomon's deviation and the Lord's punishment of him

11.0.0.en: Moabitesses and Ammonitesses: from the daughters of the peoples of Moab and the children of Ammon, who are the sons of Lot by his two daughters, and the two peoples lived east of the river Jordan.

11.0.1.en: Edomites: daughters of Edom, and Edom is Esau; his tribe lived east of the Gulf of Aqaba and south of the children of Israel.

11.0.2.en: Zidonians: daughters of Sidon, which is present-day "Saida," a famous Lebanese city on the coast of the Mediterranean.

11.0.3.en: Hittites: daughters of Heth, and it is probable that the sons of Heth are the origin of the present-day Armenians, and they lived north of the land of the Jews beside Hamath.

11.0.4.en: Solomon's heart was kindled with the love of women, and his desire led him to be joined to many wives, not only from the children of Israel but also from the peoples surrounding his country, such as the Moabitesses, the Ammonitesses, the Edomites, the Zidonians and the Hittites. What encouraged him in this was that in his days the greatness of the kings of the nations was measured by the multitude of their women, and perhaps he also intended political aims in strengthening his kingdom by being joined to the kings and leaders of these peoples.

11.0.5.en: But this was contrary to God's Law in the following respects:

11.0.7.en: 2- The Law also forbade marrying foreign women, lest they turn the people of God away from worshiping Him, so that they would be bound to the gods of the pagan nations (Ex 34:15, 16, Deut 7:3), and this is what actually happened with Solomon.

11.0.8.en: Of course the multitude of marriages made the king's expenses very great, so that Solomon's wealth did not suffice for his expenses and the treasury of the kingdom was in need, which made him increase taxes and burden his people; so he wronged and oppressed his people for the sake of his many desires.

11.0.9.en: And we notice that when God blessed Solomon and gave him many good things and wisdom, he was occupied with his desires, whereas he ought to have cared for the worship of God and the teaching of his children and his people so as to raise them spiritually, but he was content with building the house of God and then became occupied with his palaces and his desires, so he began to move away from God.

11.0.10.en: So be careful, however great your intelligence and knowledge, lest you slip into the desires of the world, by holding fast to God's commandments and submitting to your spiritual father and examining yourself every day and humbling yourself before God, and He will rescue you from the snares of the devil.

11.1.0.en: When Solomon was joined to a thousand wives, his love for God began to weaken and he moved away from the fear of God. He thought that his happiness lay in these women, so he became infatuated with them and fell under their influence.

11.1.1.en: This number of women is astonishing, and if it shows us anything, it shows that if we are lax in holding fast to the words of God and the door is opened for man's decline, it is hard for him to stop at a certain limit. Let us beware of the beginning, which may be simple but drags behind it a flood of deviations.

11.2.0.en: Solomon was influenced by the many foreign marriages, so he began to humor his wives by setting up idols for their gods, and thus in his old age he worshiped idols alongside the worship of God, and his wisdom could not protect him, because he had moved away from God and did not live with uprightness of heart, like David his father, who refused idol worship completely throughout his life. Many of the Fathers see that Solomon repented at the end of his life and wrote the Book of Ecclesiastes, which shows his renunciation of all desires and his return to the worship of God alone.

11.2.1.en: And if we say that Solomon died at about sixty years of age, then the time of his old age would be about fifty, which is an early age, but it was considered old age for him because of his great absorption in bodily pleasures and the cares and weariness that resulted from them, which made him reach old age early.

11.3.0.en: Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians: the chief goddess in both Babylon and Assyria and in the coastal cities of the Phoenicians; she was always worshiped with a male god, Baal; she and Baal were symbols of the moon and the sun.

11.3.1.en: Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites: Molech, the god of the Ammonites. Human sacrifices, especially of children, were offered to him, and his idol was made of hollow bronze, in whose cavity a fierce fire was lit, and the child was placed on the two very hot arms of the statue, while during that they beat drums to prevent his cries from being heard. Solomon allowed his Zidonian wives to worship their goddess Ashtoreth, as he allowed the Ammonite women to worship their gods Milcom, under the influence of their urging him to accept their gods. Although it is probable that he did not take part in this worship himself, but allowed it, and he may have loved it.

11.4.0.en: By this Solomon disobeyed the Lord his God and walked with other gods, and worshiped them along with the worship of the one true God, and this was evil in the sight of the Lord, who had warned him twice in two visions lest he fall into it.

11.5.0.en: Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites: the god of the Moabites. The manner of his worship was like the worship of "Molech," by offering children as sacrifices to him, and he is a sun god.

11.5.1.en: To please his wives he built a high place dedicated to the worship of the pagan god "Chemosh," god of the Moabites, and its location was the Mount of Olives, and he built another high place dedicated to the god "Molech," god of the children of Ammon. Thus the high place of Chemosh was north of Jerusalem and the high place of Molech south of it. By these high places Solomon fell into many sins:

11.5.2.en: 1- He defied God and provoked Him by setting up pagan worship in opposition to the house of God.

11.5.3.en: 2- He caused his people to stumble and led them astray, because he encouraged them to worship idols in addition to the worship of God.

11.5.4.en: 3- He made the people of God lose their standing as a good example to the surrounding nations, and God became merely one god among many gods.

11.5.5.en: And we did not hear that when Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter he set up temples for her pagan gods, and perhaps this means that he was able to convince her to worship God, so she joined his people; but his immersion in desires and the multitude of women weakened his will and his spiritual fervor, so he yielded to the pressures of his other wives and introduced their pagan worship into his country.

11.6.0.en: Solomon was not content with these two high places for pagan gods, but built the like of them for the gods of his pagan wives, who used to burn incense and sacrifice to their gods, and by this Solomon introduced idol worship and sacrificing on the high places, which remained in the life of his descendants for hundreds of years until Josiah the good king, who appeared near the end of the kingdom, that is, shortly before the captivity, and removed these forms of worship completely.

11.7.0.en: Of course Solomon's deviation into the worship of idols aroused God's anger against him, for the following reasons:

11.7.1.en: 1- Because God appeared to him twice in a vision and warned him against idol worship (ch. 3:5-14, ch. 9:1-9).

11.7.2.en: 2- God gave him wisdom that surpassed everyone before him and after him.

11.7.3.en: 3- He granted him more wealth than all the kings of the earth of his days.

11.8.0.en: God announced His punishment of Solomon because of his breaking the covenant with God and his rejecting His commandments. And He told him, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant. He means that God will permit it to be divided into two parts, and the larger part of it will be taken by Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant.

11.8.1.en: And God announced this punishment either by the hand of a prophet such as Ahijah, or by the mouth of the high priest, or in some way such as his hearing a voice from heaven.

11.9.0.en: And the honor of the saints appears: for David's sake and for the sake of the name of God called upon His Temple in Jerusalem, the holy city, God promised Solomon to postpone the punishment to the reign of his son and to leave one tribe under his rule. The one tribe mentioned is the tribe of Benjamin, which was a small tribe adjacent to the tribe of Judah, so the two joined and became one kingdom under the name of the kingdom of Judah.

11.9.1.en: And God intended by this punishment not to take vengeance on Solomon but to call him to repentance. Many of the Fathers see that he actually repented after hearing God's punishment and wrote the Book of Ecclesiastes, in which he shows the vanity of the world and his concern to keep God's commandments.

11.9.2.en: And leaving the tribe of Benjamin with Judah under the rule of David's offspring had two purposes:

11.9.3.en: 1- The continuation of the worship of God in His Temple in Jerusalem.

11.9.4.en: 2- The continuation of David's offspring until Christ, the Savior of the world, should come from it.

11.9.5.en: Be sure that God loves you even while you are in your sin, so He sends you many blessings or punishment in the form of various afflictions so that you may repent. So return to Him quickly to regain your sonship and enjoy His care and love.

11.10.0.en: The peace that surrounded Solomon during the period of his reign until now was from the arrangement of the Lord, who made all around him be at peace with him, as the Scripture says: "When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him" (Prov 16:7). But when he sinned, divine grace left him, and enemies began to appear to him who opposed him, and perhaps they had been there but were weak before the power of God that supported him; and among these enemies was Hadad the Edomite, who was an Edomite prince.

11.10.1.en: And we notice that Solomon's wealth and his concern for the multitude of horses and chariots did not protect and support him, because it is God who protects His children if they keep His commandments and stay away from desires.

11.11.0.en: To bury the slain: what is meant is the slain from the children of Israel.

11.11.1.en: David's army attacked Edom and defeated them and took their country and placed soldiers subject to him in it, but afterward Edom rebelled against David and killed some of his soldiers, so David's army attacked it under the leadership of Joab, and they buried the slain Jewish soldiers and wiped out every male in Edom, because of its rebellion, and that within six months.

11.12.0.en: Some men of the Edomite royal guard were able to flee to Egypt, and they took with them the princes, and Hadad, who was a little boy. Egypt was not on good terms with the children of Israel in the days of David as it became later in the days of Solomon, because of his marriage to Pharaoh's daughter.

11.13.0.en: Midian: a part of the Sinai Peninsula, extending from the Gulf of Aqaba to northern Sinai.

11.13.1.en: Paran: a desert south of Judah, east of Beersheba and north of Sinai.

11.13.2.en: Hadad and the men with him took an unfamiliar route in the journeys from Palestine to Egypt, to escape from David's soldiers who were pursuing them, so they went by way of "Midian" until they reached "Paran," and from there the inhabitants of Paran guided them to the way to Egypt, where they presented themselves to the king of Egypt, asking to take refuge with him, and Pharaoh was very generous with Hadad and gave him a house and assigned him daily food and gave him land.

11.14.0.en: Tahpenes: the wife of the Pharaoh who belonged to the twenty-first dynasty and was a contemporary of Solomon.

11.14.1.en: Pharaoh was impressed by Hadad, so he honored him and gave him in marriage the sister of his wife the queen, and Hadad had by her a male child whom he named "Genubath," and the child was weaned and was brought up with Pharaoh's sons in his palace. Pharaoh allied himself with Hadad by marriage so that he would be an ally to him in this region.

11.15.0.en: Hadad remained in Egypt, a fugitive from the face of David, until he learned of his death and of that of Joab the captain of his army, so he decided to return to his homeland and asked Pharaoh's permission for that, and this was in the early part of Solomon's reign, and he began to stir up the Edomites against Solomon..

11.16.0.en: Despite Pharaoh's honoring of Hadad, Hadad asked him to let him return to his country after David's death, and Pharaoh tried to keep him, but he insisted, because he wanted to avenge his country. Hadad began with weak attacks on the children of Israel at first, but they increased with time, and that was after Solomon's fall and God's punishment of him.

11.17.0.en: Hadadezer king of Zobah: David had fought him before and defeated him. He tried again with the help of other kings who allied with him, and David defeated them also and slew their commander "Shobach," and the rest submitted to David (2 Sam 10:6-19). Zobah: a great kingdom among the kingdoms of "Aram" west of the Euphrates.

11.17.1.en: The second adversary was Rezon the son of Eliadah, one of the commanders of Hadadezer king of Zobah, who fled after David defeated them, and Rezon and all who were with him continued to fear David because of his godliness and God's support of him, and then after him Solomon, when he worshiped God with all his heart. But when Solomon turned aside to the worship of idols, God withdrew His support from him, and Rezon began to oppose Solomon.

11.18.0.en: When Rezon fled from the face of David, he formed a band to which he gathered many men, and he began to attack some countries and take their spoils until he grew strong and was able to attack Damascus and take possession of it.

11.19.1.en: By Rezon's reigning over Damascus he gained control of the kingdom of Aram, whose capital is Damascus. Damascus was a commercial city on a trade route, and by Rezon's reigning over it Solomon lost much in his trade, and Aram was no longer subject to him but became a center of opposition to him from the north of his country, in addition to the opposition of Hadad the Edomite to him from the south (v. 14). And Rezon bore hatred for Solomon because of what David had done in his country, so he opposed Solomon fiercely.

11.19.2.en: Keep God's commandments so that He may keep you from your enemies the demons, who want to devour you but fear you if you hold fast to God. So trust in your strength as long as you are with God, and do not be concerned about the threats of the wicked, for God is able to rescue you from them.

11.20.s.en: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

11.20.0.en: Zeredah: a city located west of the Jordan.

11.20.1.en: A third adversary of Solomon appeared, Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was one of his servants and was from the tribe of Ephraim and from the city of Zeredah; his mother's name was Zeruah and she was a widow. The tribe of Ephraim was the largest of the tribes in number and was much given to rebellion since the era of the judges, in the days of Gideon and after him Jephthah the Gileadite, and then they rebelled against David. Thus enemies of Solomon appear not only from outside, like Hadad and Rezon, but also from within, that is, from his servants.

11.21.0.en: Lifted up his hand against the king: rebelled against him.

11.21.1.en: The story of Jeroboam's rebellion began from the time Solomon built Millo, which is a fortified part of Jerusalem, and repaired the city of David also, which is another part of Jerusalem. Jeroboam's industry in work and strong personality appeared, so that Solomon trusted him and appointed him over the workers from the house of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, because he was an Ephraimite like them. And Jeroboam was strong in his leadership of the tribe of Ephraim, because forced labor is a hated thing, in addition to the tribe of Ephraim feeling that it had more right to the kingship than the tribe of Judah from which Solomon came. So how could they be subjected to forced labor for a king who was not of their tribe?

11.22.0.en: Shiloh: located in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Jerusalem at a distance of 19 km, and it was the seat of the tabernacle of meeting for a long time, from the days of Joshua until David (Josh 18:1). It happened at that time that Jeroboam was going out of the city of Jerusalem, probably to carry out some mission he had been charged with, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him, and the prophet was wearing a new garment. The prophet took off the garment he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces, according to the number of the tribes of Israel. And in order that God might declare that He is the one who made the decision to tear the kingdom, He had His prophet, who represents Him, tear his garment into twelve pieces, that is, God, the true King of the kingdom, would permit it to be torn into two parts, the first including ten tribes and the second two tribes. This reminds us of what Saul did when he caught hold of Samuel's garment and it tore, and then Samuel said that God would tear the kingdom from him, that is, Saul would die and one who deserves it, David, would reign over it (1 Sam 15:27, 28).

11.23.0.en: The prophet said to Jeroboam, Take ten pieces of this garment, and then explained to him what that means, namely that the Lord, the God of Israel, would permit the kingdom of Israel to be divided, after all the tribes had been subject to Solomon, and that Jeroboam would take ten tribes to reign over.

11.24.0.en: But because of the Lord's love for David and His esteem for Jerusalem, the city chosen for His name to be upon it, He decided to keep one tribe continuing in submission to Solomon, the tribe of Benjamin, in addition to the tribe of Judah from which Solomon came.

11.25.0.en: The Lord declared the reason for His permitting the tearing of the kingdom, which is Israel's forsaking the living God and their worshiping Ashtoreth the god of Sidon, and Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and thus Israel had turned aside, under Solomon's rule, from the way of the Lord, and had not done what is pleasing to the Lord and had not kept the statutes and judgments that He had given it as it had kept them during the reign of David. And because of Solomon's concern for the pagan gods, he caused many of his people to fall into idol worship.

11.25.1.en: When a trial comes upon you, examine yourself lest the cause be your sin, and repent of it, and know that God is compassionate and ready to forgive you and remove the trial from you and turn it to your good.

11.26.0.en: Again the Lord declares His faithfulness to His covenants to David and His love for him, in that the separation of the tribes would not take place in Solomon's lifetime, but He would leave him king over all the tribes of the children of Israel all the days of his life. Perhaps God wants by this to give him a chance to repent and not be occupied with the division of the kingdom in his days, for God appreciates Solomon's labors in building the Temple and all his great works. And Solomon most likely repented, as proved by his writing the Book of Ecclesiastes at the end of his life, but God insisted on the division of the kingdom because of the spread of idol worship in which many of the kings who were of Solomon's offspring walked.

11.27.0.en: The Lord repeats mention of what He will do in the future, that this division would take place in the days of the reign of Solomon's son, and the Lord would give ten tribes to Jeroboam to reign over.

11.28.0.en: The Lord leaves one tribe so that the remembrance of David may remain before Him all the days in the city of Jerusalem, which He chose to put His name there, and Jerusalem did not fall into captivity until the end, after all the tribes. And as David was a shining star in God's hand, so his offspring will be a lamp throughout the days, and even if some of his offspring walked in evil and the light of the lamp grew dim in those times, yet this lamp shines mightily in the person of Christ, who comes from the offspring of David to reign forever over the hearts of those who believe in Him.

11.29.0.en: The Lord gives the kingship to Jeroboam and grants him all that he desires, and he will be king over Israel. We see here that God announces the name of the new, split-off kingdom, that is, of the ten tribes, which is the kingdom of Israel, and God knew that Jeroboam desired the kingship and that his whole tribe desired the kingship, so He gave him this kingship, but on condition of submission to His commandments (v. 38).

11.30.0.en: Here the Lord sets for Jeroboam a condition for the continuance of His blessing to him, which is keeping the commandment and walking in the ways of the Lord and doing what is right in His eyes, with observing the statutes and ordinances of the Law, as David did before, and then the hand of the Lord would be with him, so He would bring stability to the kingdom and establish him in the rule of Israel, he and his offspring after him. Although God knows by His foreknowledge that Jeroboam is wicked and will worship idols, yet He commands him, in the hope that he may believe and live with God.

11.31.0.en: And if God will humble the offspring of David for their sins, not only by their having a small kingdom, the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin only, but also by His permitting them to be disciplined in captivity, yet the captivity will not continue all the days, but they will return from it and unite again with the rest of the tribes; and then He gives them hope also that this humiliation will end with the birth of Christ and His salvation of mankind, that is, the true offspring of David, who are all the believers.

11.32.0.en: Solomon learned of Ahijah's prophecy to Jeroboam, so he asked for Jeroboam to be arrested in order to kill him, and Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt. The strange thing is that Solomon did not repent before this prophecy, and all he tried was to kill Jeroboam, and of course he could not, because the prophecy is from God.

11.32.1.en: And it is understood from (v. 26) that Jeroboam, after hearing Ahijah's prophecy, became proud, and perhaps he gathered around him some troublemakers and rebels against Solomon and began to declare his rebellion against the king. This is what made Solomon seek to kill him, which shows the extent of Jeroboam's pride, impulsiveness and wickedness; for God permitted Jeroboam's reigning as a discipline for His people who worshiped idols, perhaps that they might repent.

11.33.0.en: The writer of the book refers here to other details concerning what Solomon did during the period of his reign and his wisdom for which he was famous, and these details are recorded in a book called "the acts of Solomon," a historical book, perhaps the chronicles that the kings write for themselves, or that someone wrote about the history of Solomon, and it is different from the books recorded in the Bible.

11.34.0.en: The period of Solomon's reign in Jerusalem over all Israel was 40 years, after which Solomon died and was buried in the city of David his father, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his stead. Solomon's age at his death did not exceed sixty, because the Fathers say that he was anointed king while young, and in all likelihood he had not passed twenty. And although his father David endured many troubles from Saul and suffered from various wars with the surrounding nations in addition to troubles from his children, God blessed him and gave him peace of heart and he reigned 40 years, but he lived longer than Solomon, for God gave him a life of seventy years.

11.34.1.en: Thus we find that Solomon fell into many errors and received punishment from the very same sins and arising from them, as appears in the following:

11.34.2.en: 1- He multiplied the acquiring of horses, contrary to the Law, so the horses and chariots of the enemies attacked the kingdom in the reign of his son Rehoboam.

11.34.3.en: 2- He acquired much gold that the enemies desired, so they attacked the kingdom after his death in various ages and took it.

11.34.4.en: 3- He multiplied marriages, and they turned his heart to the worship of idols, so he set up forms of worship for them in Jerusalem and around it and by this led his people astray, and the Lord was angry with him.

11.34.5.en: 4- He used forced labor, hated by the people, to carry out his huge projects, so his people were troubled and killed Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, and rose up against Rehoboam his son, and the kingdom was divided by the hand of Jeroboam, who had been in charge of the forced labor.

11.34.6.en: Do not be drawn to the desire of sin and its pleasures, lest you be struck by its punishment that results from it, in addition to God's anger against you, so that you lose your peace and forfeit your eternity. And if you fall, return to God by repentance so that you do not remain in your error after the devil.
